VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

Legal-approved disclosure language - Q3 FY2026 (approved by K. Brandt, General Counsel, 12 Oct 2026)
For use in shareholder letter and prepared remarks. Use verbatim; do not paraphrase.

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Our third quarter showed the strength of our data-center cooling franchise alongside continued pressure in our core commercial business. Total backlog reached a record $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year, led by Thermal & Data Center Solutions, where backlog grew 22.0% to $574.2 million and we won two hyperscale awards. Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales rose 13.4% to $156.3 million. Building Controls & Valves remained soft, and we moved quickly and put customers first in addressing a voluntary field action in that segment. Adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. On a GAAP basis we reported a net loss of $15.6 million, or $(0.37) per diluted share, which includes recall-related and restructuring charges.

## Highlights

- Record total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year; data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0%.
- Two hyperscale awards in Thermal & Data Center Solutions, adding liquid-cooling content into FY2027 and beyond.
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million, now 37.9% of total net sales.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS of $0.15; GAAP net loss of $15.6 million, or $(0.37) per diluted share.
- Voluntary GV-400 field action filed with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program; corrective action complete and replacement valves shipping.
- Project Keystone on track to deliver $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% year over year, driven by liquid-cooling demand from hyperscale and colocation customers. The CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger continued to ramp with the two hyperscale customers we announced in the second quarter, and we won two further hyperscale awards during the period, extending our content across both new and existing data-center platforms. Order intake continued to outpace revenue, lifting data-center backlog 22.0% to $574.2 million. That backlog is the clearest signal we have of where this business is going, and it gives us strong visibility into FY2027.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year, reflecting continued softness in non-residential construction and lower OEM volumes. During the quarter we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves sold to OEM customers for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters, working with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program. Our teams identified the root cause — an out-of-specification diaphragm compound from a supplier change made in 2025 — corrected it, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant on September 28. No injuries have been reported. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. Three OEM customers, including our second-largest BCV customer, have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice, and that pause is reflected in our updated outlook.

This was a voluntary, proactive, customer-first action, taken with the CPSC under the Fast Track program and notified to Health Canada. We take this seriously, and we take confidence in the response: root cause identified, corrective action complete, replacement parts flowing, and no injuries reported. Quality and product safety sit at the top of our operating agenda, and the lessons from this field action are being applied across our sourcing and supplier-quality processes.

## Outlook

Net sales for the quarter were $412.6 million, down 6.0% year over year. We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million. The update reflects the pace of recovery in BCV end markets and the temporary pause in GV-400 orders; it does not change the momentum we see in data-center cooling, where backlog conversion supports growth into FY2027.

Cost actions are accelerating. Project Keystone actions taken in the third quarter are expected to reach a $35 million run-rate by the end of Q2 FY2027, with benefits building through FY2027 across procurement, footprint and overhead. Together with richer TDC mix, these actions underpin the margin recovery we expect as volumes return.

Free cash flow in the quarter was $(11.3) million, and capital expenditures were $14.9 million, weighted to data-center assembly and test capacity. Our capital priorities are unchanged: first, fund the liquid-cooling ramp; second, strengthen the balance sheet as backlog converts and savings land. Working capital discipline — inventory and receivables — is a specific focus for the balance of the year.

We thank our OEM customers for their partnership through the recall, and our data-center customers for the confidence reflected in a record backlog.
